slides.title: The nurse on the CQI committee is developing a program to reduce medication erro
text: Question: The nurse on the CQI committee is developing a program to reduce medication errors after a sentinel event. Which strategy should the committee initiate first?
A. Identify key performance indicators (KPIs) of the medication error.
B. Review the events that led to the error by creating a flow diagram.
C. Provide an inservice to staff on safe medication administration.
D. Develop a quality improvement program for nurses involved in the error.
Correct answer: B. Review the events that led to the error by creating a flow diagram.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:

Understand the problem before acting. Mapping the process (flow diagram/root-cause analysis) shows where the system failed. Education and programs follow, and the focus is on systems, not blaming individuals.

slides.title: The nurse attended a conference on informed consent. Which statement indicates c
text: Question: The nurse attended a conference on informed consent. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
A. Informed consent can be waived per facility policy for urgent treatment if the client is unconscious.
B. Informed consent may not be withdrawn once the client signs.
C. Informed consent can be signed by a client with dementia if oriented at the time of signing.
D. Informed consent is signed by the nurse to indicate the client understands.
Correct answer: A. Informed consent can be waived per facility policy for urgent treatment if the client is unconscious.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:

Emergency (implied) consent applies when delay would risk life or limb and the client cannot consent. Consent can be withdrawn at any time, the client must be competent, and the nurse witnesses the signature but the provider explains the procedure.

slides.title: After hand-off report, the nurse should first see the client who
text: Question: After hand-off report, the nurse should first see the client who
A. has pancreatitis and reports mid-epigastric discomfort.
B. had a transesophageal echocardiogram 2 hours ago, BP 106/64, with a sore throat.
C. has cirrhosis, new ecchymosis, and PTT 76 seconds.
D. had a laparoscopic cholecystectomy 18 hours ago with bilateral shoulder pain.
Correct answer: C. has cirrhosis, new ecchymosis, and PTT 76 seconds.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:

A PTT of 76 s (normal 25–35) with new bruising means active bleeding risk and a coagulation problem in cirrhosis. Epigastric discomfort, post-TEE sore throat, and shoulder pain from retained CO₂ after laparoscopy are expected.

slides.title: Clients are 24 hours postoperative; the nurse assessed 4 hours ago. Which change
text: Question: Clients are 24 hours postoperative; the nurse assessed 4 hours ago. Which change is a priority?
A. Received NPH insulin and capillary glucose is 110 mg/dL.
B. Wound drainage was sanguineous and is now serosanguineous.
C. BP was 138/86 and is now 136/84.
D. Reports pain increased to 8/10 after an opioid analgesic.
Correct answer: D. Reports pain increased to 8/10 after an opioid analgesic.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:
Pain that worsens after an opioid can signal a complication (bleeding, ischemia, compartment syndrome, anastomotic leak). The other changes are normal or insignificant.

slides.title: The preceptor is teaching legal principles. Which situation is an example of mal
text: Question: The preceptor is teaching legal principles. Which situation is an example of malpractice?
A. An alert client leaves AMA; the nurse applies restraints to prevent leaving.
B. A competent client refuses an antidepressant; the nurse dissolves it in food and gives it without the client’s knowledge.
C. The nurse plugs in an alarming IV pump despite noticing a loose outlet cover.
D. A client on a low-sodium diet eats chips; the nurse threatens wrist restraints.
Correct answer: B. A competent client refuses an antidepressant; the nurse dissolves it in food and gives it without the client’s knowledge.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Giving medication covertly violates the client’s right to refuse treatment and falls below the standard of care. Items A and D are false imprisonment/assault concerns. (Key per source.)

slides.title: It is a priority for the nurse to follow up with a client who
text: Question: It is a priority for the nurse to follow up with a client who
A. is receiving hydrocortisone and has glucose 135 mg/dL.
B. has MS, feels tired, and has diplopia.
C. has active pulmonary TB, hemoptysis, and weight loss.
D. is receiving pyridostigmine and reports nausea and a congested cough.
Correct answer: D. is receiving pyridostigmine and reports nausea and a congested cough.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:
Nausea and increased secretions on an anticholinesterase suggest cholinergic crisis (overmedication). This can progress to respiratory failure. The other findings are expected in those diagnoses.

slides.title: On a pediatric cardiac unit, which client should the nurse initially assess?
text: Question: On a pediatric cardiac unit, which client should the nurse initially assess?
A. 5-year-old watching TV with a pulse of 78.
B. Toddler playing with toys with a pulse of 100.
C. 1-month-old sleeping with a pulse of 180.
D. 15-year-old reading with a pulse of 60.
Correct answer: C. 1-month-old sleeping with a pulse of 180.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
An infant’s normal rate is ~100–160, lower when asleep. 180 while sleeping is tachycardia. The other rates are normal.

slides.title: Which child should receive an interdisciplinary conference?
text: Question: Which child should receive an interdisciplinary conference?
A. 3 years old, epiglottitis, difficulty breathing.
B. 4 years old, new Kawasaki disease, started on immunoglobulin.
C. 8 years old, multiple compound fractures in Buck’s traction.
D. 5 years old, cystic fibrosis since birth, hospitalized 4 times in 2 months.
Correct answer: D. 5 years old, cystic fibrosis since birth, hospitalized 4 times in 2 months.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
A chronic, complex illness with repeated admissions needs a team approach (respiratory therapy, dietitian, PT, social work, spiritual care). Others are acute or have a single-discipline focus.

slides.title: A client with pericarditis has been hospitalized for 24 hours. WBC 13,000/mm³ an
text: Question: A client with pericarditis has been hospitalized for 24 hours. WBC 13,000/mm³ and temperature 100.8° F. What is the most appropriate action?
A. Update the nursing interventions as needed.
B. Notify the charge nurse that the plan of care is outdated.
C. Change the client’s goal to reflect current status.
D. Obtain an order for an infectious disease referral.
Correct answer: A. Update the nursing interventions as needed.
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:
These findings fit the inflammatory process of pericarditis. Evaluation of the plan means modifying interventions (e.g., fever/comfort measures), not changing goals or escalating.

slides.title: Which charted note by a nurse indicates correct documentation?
text: Question: Which charted note by a nurse indicates correct documentation?
A. “Dressing change performed to coccyx wound with no adverse effects noted by the client. Client transferred to chair.”
B. “IV catheter site in left antecubital space is red and warm to touch. IV catheter removed intact. 20-gauge catheter placed in right forearm.”
C. “Found client sitting on floor. All 4 side rails upright. Client reports no pain. No abrasions or bleeding. PHCP notified. Incident report completed.”
D. “Reports of pain in abdomen with vomiting noted. Medications administered.”
Correct answer: B. “IV catheter site in left antecubital space is red and warm to touch. IV catheter removed intact. 20-gauge catheter placed in right forearm.”
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:

Document objective, specific, factual details (site, assessment findings, gauge, location). Don’t mention incident reports in the chart, and avoid vague wording (“no adverse effects,” “medications administered”).

slides.title: A client brought in their own CPAP machine. What is the most important nurse act
text: Question: A client brought in their own CPAP machine. What is the most important nurse action?
A. Explain that the hospital must supply the CPAP machine.
B. Review the instruction booklet on how to operate the machine.
C. Ask the client when they last cleaned the machine.
D. Have the machine inspected by the facility’s engineering department.
Correct answer: D. Have the machine inspected by the facility’s engineering department.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Client-owned electrical equipment must be checked for electrical safety by biomedical/engineering before use.

slides.title: The facility’s emergency response plan is activated. Which client should the nur
text: Question: The facility’s emergency response plan is activated. Which client should the nurse recommend for discharge?
A. DVT on warfarin with PT 28 seconds.
B. HIV positive, nonproductive cough, Mantoux 6 mm induration.
C. Suspected appendicitis with intense McBurney’s point pain, now reporting the pain has stopped.
D. COPD on IV steroids with SpO₂ 86% on room air.
Correct answer: A. DVT on warfarin with PT 28 seconds.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:

Discharge the most stable client. A PT of 28 s (about 2× normal) is therapeutic on warfarin. Sudden pain relief in appendicitis suggests rupture, 6 mm in an HIV+ client is positive, and SpO₂ 86% is unstable.

slides.title: The nurse observes a newly hired UAP. Which action indicates correct care?
text: Question: The nurse observes a newly hired UAP. Which action indicates correct care?
A. Wearing a gown to enter the room of a client with influenza.
B. Removing protective eyewear before removing gloves.
C. Placing dedicated equipment in the room of a client with herpes zoster.
D. Donning sterile gloves to empty a urinary drainage device.
Correct answer: C. Placing dedicated equipment in the room of a client with herpes zoster.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Herpes zoster requires contact precautions, including dedicated equipment. Influenza = droplet (mask). Gloves come off FIRST (most contaminated), and clean gloves are used to empty drainage devices.

slides.title: During a class on child car passenger safety, which parent statement indicates a
text: Question: During a class on child car passenger safety, which parent statement indicates a need for further teaching?
A. “Car seats should be rear-facing in the back seat until about 2 to 4 years.”
B. “With a booster seat, the lap belt should be across the child’s upper thighs.”
C. “The harness chest clip should be at the level of the infant’s armpits.”
D. “One hand should fit between the infant and the harness.”
Correct answer: D. “One hand should fit between the infant and the harness.”
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
The harness should be snug: no more than one to two fingers should fit beneath it. A whole hand means it is too loose.

slides.title: Which new order requires follow-up by the nurse?
text: Question: Which new order requires follow-up by the nurse?
A. Fluid bolus of 500 mL over 1 hour for a 12-year-old in sickle cell crisis.
B. High-potassium diet for a 5-year-old with acute glomerulonephritis.
C. Chelation therapy for an 8-year-old with lead poisoning.
D. IV hydrocortisone for a 10-year-old with adrenal insufficiency.
Correct answer: B. High-potassium diet for a 5-year-old with acute glomerulonephritis.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Acute glomerulonephritis causes oliguria and hyperkalemia, so potassium, sodium, and fluids are restricted. The other orders are appropriate.

slides.title: Which order should the nurse clarify?
text: Question: Which order should the nurse clarify?
A. IV alteplase for ischemic stroke symptoms that began 2 hours ago.
B. Low-sodium, low-potassium diet for acute kidney injury.
C. Chest x-ray for a client with a permanent pacemaker placed 6 months ago.
D. 1 unit of PRBCs for a client with polycythemia vera.
Correct answer: D. 1 unit of PRBCs for a client with polycythemia vera.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Polycythemia vera is an excess of RBCs, so transfusing more would increase viscosity and clotting risk. X-rays are safe with pacemakers; MRI is the concern.

slides.title: Oxytocin is infusing for labor augmentation. The nurse should discontinue it if
text: Question: Oxytocin is infusing for labor augmentation. The nurse should discontinue it if the client has
A. uterine relaxation between contractions.
B. an FHR of 68 for 90 seconds.
C. dark red streaks in the bloody show.
D. intermittent back pain with each contraction.
Correct answer: B. an FHR of 68 for 90 seconds.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Fetal bradycardia indicates fetal distress or uterine hyperstimulation. Stop oxytocin, turn the client left, give oxygen, and notify the provider. Relaxation between contractions is desired.

slides.title: After ensuring a newborn has a patent airway, what should the nurse do next?
text: Question: After ensuring a newborn has a patent airway, what should the nurse do next?
A. Weigh the newborn and document the weight.
B. Dry the newborn’s skin and cover with a warm blanket.
C. Administer vitamin K.
D. Administer eye prophylaxis.
Correct answer: B. Dry the newborn’s skin and cover with a warm blanket.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
After airway comes thermoregulation (ABC then temperature). Cold stress increases oxygen consumption and hypoglycemia. Weight, vitamin K and eye care follow.

slides.title: The nurse is auscultating the aortic valve. The diagram shows four sites: (1) ri
text: Question: The nurse is auscultating the aortic valve. The diagram shows four sites: (1) right 2nd intercostal space at the sternal border, (2) left 2nd intercostal space at the sternal border, (3) left 4th intercostal space at the sternal border, (4) left 5th intercostal space at the midclavicular line. Where should the stethoscope be placed?
A. Site 1: right 2nd intercostal space, sternal border.
B. Site 2: left 2nd intercostal space, sternal border.
C. Site 3: left 4th intercostal space, sternal border.
D. Site 4: left 5th intercostal space, midclavicular line.
Correct answer: A. Site 1: right 2nd intercostal space, sternal border.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Aortic = right 2nd ICS (“Aortic Right”). Pulmonic = left 2nd ICS. Tricuspid = left lower sternal border. Mitral (apical) = 5th ICS midclavicular line. (Diagram was an image in your PDF.)

slides.title: A client with AB-negative blood delivered a baby 4 hours ago. Which action shoul
text: Question: A client with AB-negative blood delivered a baby 4 hours ago. Which action should the nurse be prepared to take?
A. Assess the newborn for abnormal clotting.
B. Administer Rh(D) immune globulin to the infant after double-nurse verification.
C. Review the newborn’s blood type.
D. Administer Rh(D) immune globulin to the mother within 24 hours of birth.
Correct answer: C. Review the newborn’s blood type.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Rh(D) immune globulin is given to the Rh-NEGATIVE mother only if the newborn is Rh-POSITIVE, so check the newborn’s type first. It is given to the mother within 72 hours (not the infant).

slides.title: LMP began November 19. Using Naegele’s rule, what is the EDD?
text: Question: LMP began November 19. Using Naegele’s rule, what is the EDD?
A. July 12
B. August 12
C. July 26
D. August 26
Correct answer: D. August 26
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Naegele’s rule: add 7 days to the LMP and subtract 3 months. Nov 19 + 7 = Nov 26 → minus 3 months = August 26.

slides.title: A client who had a below-the-knee amputation from diabetic circulation problems
text: Question: A client who had a below-the-knee amputation from diabetic circulation problems shows ineffective coping with defense mechanisms. Which action should the nurse take?
A. Determine what is causing the client to respond in such a way.
B. Obtain an order for a psychiatric consultation.
C. Tell the client their behavior is not acceptable.
D. Explain that their reactions are unproductive to getting better.
Correct answer: A. Determine what is causing the client to respond in such a way.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Assess first (nursing process) with open, nonjudgmental exploration. Defense mechanisms are normal reactions to loss. Avoid judging or lecturing.

slides.title: A client presents to the ED after an amitriptyline overdose. Which action should
text: Question: A client presents to the ED after an amitriptyline overdose. Which action should the nurse take first?
A. Administer oxygen via nasal cannula.
B. Initiate gastric lavage with activated charcoal.
C. Determine the events leading to the overdose.
D. Document the number of pills ingested.
Correct answer: A. Administer oxygen via nasal cannula.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
ABCs come first: TCA overdose causes respiratory depression, arrhythmias, and seizures. Support airway/breathing before decontamination or history-taking.

Conflicting answer: the same question in the outside (not Galen) set "Comp C Highlights" gives a different answer: "Initiate gastric lavage with activated charcoal.". Yours here is "Administer oxygen via nasal cannula.". The two keys cannot both be what your instructor wants; check this one against your class materials.

slides.title: On a mental health unit, the nurse should first assess the client who has
text: Question: On a mental health unit, the nurse should first assess the client who has
A. paranoid schizophrenia and has not bathed in 3 days.
B. major depressive disorder stating, “I wish I could stop crying all the time.”
C. bulimia nervosa and went to the restroom 15 minutes after a meal.
D. suicidal ideation and is reluctantly discussing a suicide contract with staff.
Correct answer: C. bulimia nervosa and went to the restroom 15 minutes after a meal.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Active purging (vomiting) risks electrolyte imbalance (hypokalemia) and cardiac arrhythmias. The suicidal client is already engaged with staff in safety planning, and the others are not urgent.

Conflicting answer: the same question in the outside (not Galen) set "Comp C Highlights" gives a different answer: "Suicidal ideations and is reluctantly discussing a suicide contract with a staff member.". Yours here is "bulimia nervosa and went to the restroom 15 minutes after a meal.". The two keys cannot both be what your instructor wants; check this one against your class materials.

slides.title: Which client is at highest risk for suicide?
text: Question: Which client is at highest risk for suicide?
A. 70-year-old man whose wife recently died and goes to weekly bingo with friends.
B. 52-year-old man who lost his job 3 months ago and feels he will never find another.
C. 39-year-old woman newly diagnosed with breast cancer seeking a second opinion.
D. 15-year-old girl who just broke up with her boyfriend and spends more time with friends.
Correct answer: B. 52-year-old man who lost his job 3 months ago and feels he will never find another.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Hopelessness plus a major loss in a middle-aged man is a strong risk profile. The others still have social connection and active coping.

slides.title: A newly hired nurse is giving continuous tube feeding via a gastrostomy tube. Wh
text: Question: A newly hired nurse is giving continuous tube feeding via a gastrostomy tube. Which action requires immediate intervention?
A. Adding no more than 4 hours’ worth of feeding to the bag.
B. Keeping the HOB at 30–45 degrees.
C. Using an irrigation set opened 48 hours ago.
D. Returning the residual obtained from the tube.
Correct answer: C. Using an irrigation set opened 48 hours ago.
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
Irrigation sets are changed every 24 hours to prevent bacterial contamination. Limiting formula to 4 hours, a 30–45° HOB, and returning residuals are acceptable.

slides.title: A client with urinary incontinence is at risk for skin breakdown. Which preventi
text: Question: A client with urinary incontinence is at risk for skin breakdown. Which preventive action should the nurse implement?
A. Check the skin every 8 hours.
B. Request an order for an indwelling catheter.
C. Clean the perineum with hot water after each episode.
D. Apply a moisture barrier ointment to the skin.
Correct answer: D. Apply a moisture barrier ointment to the skin.
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
Barrier ointment protects skin from urine. Check and cleanse after each episode with warm water and pH-balanced cleanser. Catheters are not used for convenience (CAUTI risk).

slides.title: Which action should the nurse take when caring for a client in Buck’s (skin) tra
text: Question: Which action should the nurse take when caring for a client in Buck’s (skin) traction?
A. Turn the client to a 30-degree angle every 2 hours.
B. Provide pin site care.
C. Assess pedal push strength every 4 hours.
D. Keep the foot of the bed elevated.
Correct answer: D. Keep the foot of the bed elevated.
Topic: Neuro, Eyes & Ortho
notes: Rationale:
Buck’s traction needs countertraction: elevate the foot of the bed so the client’s body weight pulls back against the traction. Pin care applies to skeletal traction.

Conflicting answer: the same question in the outside (not Galen) set "Comp C Highlights" gives a different answer: "Assess pedal pulse strength every 4 hours.". Yours here is "Keep the foot of the bed elevated.". The two keys cannot both be what your instructor wants; check this one against your class materials.

slides.title: When assessing an older adult for urinary incontinence, which question is import
text: Question: When assessing an older adult for urinary incontinence, which question is important?
A. “Do you take the herbal preparation ginkgo biloba?”
B. “Do you ever use pads or tissues in your underwear to catch urine?”
C. “Do you have a history of kidney stones?”
D. “Do you have a family history of polycystic kidney disease?”
Correct answer: B. “Do you ever use pads or tissues in your underwear to catch urine?”
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
Asking about pads/tissues reveals the extent, frequency, and impact of incontinence, which is essential for planning care.

slides.title: A client with a UTI has been prescribed ciprofloxacin. Which instruction should
text: Question: A client with a UTI has been prescribed ciprofloxacin. Which instruction should the nurse give?
A. “This medication provides an analgesic effect and decreases painful urination.”
B. “Antacids should be taken 30 minutes after this medication.”
C. “You should not operate heavy machinery or drive while taking this medication.”
D. “You could experience dizziness and should change positions slowly.”
Correct answer: D. “You could experience dizziness and should change positions slowly.”
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:

Fluoroquinolones can cause dizziness, lightheadedness, and CNS effects, so teach safety and slow position changes. Also report tendon pain (rupture risk), and separate from antacids/iron/calcium by 2+ hours.

slides.title: An older adult takes furosemide daily for heart failure. Which finding is a prio
text: Question: An older adult takes furosemide daily for heart failure. Which finding is a priority to follow up?
A. Reports of ringing in the ears.
B. Orientation to person and place only.
C. Potassium level of 3.5 mEq/L.
D. Weight loss of 1 lb in 3 days.
Correct answer: A. Reports of ringing in the ears.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Tinnitus signals ototoxicity, which can become permanent with loop diuretics, so report it before further doses. Potassium 3.5 is low-normal and a 1 lb loss is expected. (Key per source.)

slides.title: A 22-year-old female is prescribed lithium. Which statement needs further teachi
text: Question: A 22-year-old female is prescribed lithium. Which statement needs further teaching?
A. “I should be sure to eat food that contains sodium.”
B. “I should take this medication with food.”
C. “This medication will make my urine turn reddish-orange.”
D. “I should avoid becoming dehydrated.”
Correct answer: C. “This medication will make my urine turn reddish-orange.”
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Lithium does not discolor urine (that’s phenazopyridine/rifampin). Maintain steady sodium and fluid intake, because low sodium or dehydration raises lithium to toxic levels.

slides.title: A client’s potassium is 2.4 mEq/L. Which order should the nurse question?
text: Question: A client’s potassium is 2.4 mEq/L. Which order should the nurse question?
A. Administer 20 mEq KCl IV over 15 minutes.
B. Withhold the regularly scheduled furosemide.
C. Place the client on telemetry.
D. Allow the client out of bed with assistance only.
Correct answer: A. Administer 20 mEq KCl IV over 15 minutes.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
IV potassium must not exceed 10 mEq/hr on a general unit (rapid infusion can cause cardiac arrest). Telemetry, holding furosemide, and fall precautions are appropriate.

slides.title: Which prescription should the nurse follow up with the PHCP?
text: Question: Which prescription should the nurse follow up with the PHCP?
A. Aspirin sensitivity and prescribed acetaminophen.
B. Potassium 3.8 mEq/L and prescribed sodium polystyrene.
C. Decreased phenytoin level and prescribed seizure precautions.
D. History of rash with penicillin and prescribed an MAOI.
Correct answer: B. Potassium 3.8 mEq/L and prescribed sodium polystyrene.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Sodium polystyrene lowers potassium and is for hyperkalemia. A normal K⁺ of 3.8 could cause hypokalemia. The other orders are appropriate (the penicillin rash is unrelated to MAOIs).

slides.title: The nurse is teaching a client with anemia who is starting liquid ferrous sulfat
text: Question: The nurse is teaching a client with anemia who is starting liquid ferrous sulfate. Which instruction should be included?
A. “Avoid eating excessive amounts of beans and green leafy vegetables.”
B. “You will notice a change in your bowel habits and stool color.”
C. “The medication can be taken with milk to prevent GI irritation.”
D. “Do not mix the medication with any other medications, foods, or liquids.”
Correct answer: B. “You will notice a change in your bowel habits and stool color.”
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Iron causes dark green/black stools and constipation or GI upset. Dilute liquid iron, use a straw to avoid staining teeth, and avoid milk/antacids that reduce absorption.

slides.title: The nurse will give subcutaneous enoxaparin. Which action should the nurse take?
text: Question: The nurse will give subcutaneous enoxaparin. Which action should the nurse take?
A. Check the most current D-dimer.
B. Gently massage the area after administration.
C. Aspirate for blood before injecting.
D. Insert the needle at a 90-degree angle.
Correct answer: D. Insert the needle at a 90-degree angle.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Enoxaparin is given in the abdomen at 90°. Don’t aspirate, expel the air bubble, or massage (bruising/hematoma). Monitor platelets/CBC, not D-dimer.

slides.title: A toddler who weighs 22 lb is prescribed ampicillin 150 mg PO three times daily.
text: Question: A toddler who weighs 22 lb is prescribed ampicillin 150 mg PO three times daily. Available: suspension 250 mg/5 mL. What should the nurse do?
A. Check for an allergy to sulfa medications.
B. Contact the PHCP for clarification.
C. Administer 3 mL by mouth 3 times per day.
D. Determine the toddler’s weight in kilograms.
Correct answer: C. Administer 3 mL by mouth 3 times per day.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Do the math: 150 mg ÷ 250 mg × 5 mL = 3 mL per dose. The question supplies what is needed, so no clarification is required (22 lb ≈ 10 kg).

Conflicting answer: the same question in the outside (not Galen) set "Comp C Highlights" gives a different answer: "Determine the toddler’s weight in kilograms.". Yours here is "Administer 3 mL by mouth 3 times per day.". The two keys cannot both be what your instructor wants; check this one against your class materials.

slides.title: After a paracentesis, it is a priority to notify the PHCP if the client develops
text: Question: After a paracentesis, it is a priority to notify the PHCP if the client develops
A. pink-tinged urine.
B. vesicular breath sounds.
C. flatulence.
D. pruritus.
Correct answer: A. pink-tinged urine.
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
Pink-tinged urine (hematuria) suggests bladder puncture/perforation. Vesicular breath sounds are normal, and expected findings include drainage at the site and decreased abdominal girth.

Conflicting answer: the same question in the outside (not Galen) set "Comp C Highlights" gives a different answer: "Pruritus.". Yours here is "pink-tinged urine.". The two keys cannot both be what your instructor wants; check this one against your class materials.

slides.title: ABG: pH 7.52, PaCO₂ 26 mm Hg, HCO₃⁻ 24 mEq/L. Which acid-base imbalance?
text: Question: ABG: pH 7.52, PaCO₂ 26 mm Hg, HCO₃⁻ 24 mEq/L. Which acid-base imbalance?
A. Respiratory acidosis
B. Metabolic acidosis
C. Respiratory alkalosis
D. Metabolic alkalosis
Correct answer: C. Respiratory alkalosis
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
High pH (alkalosis) with LOW CO₂ (respiratory cause) and normal bicarbonate = respiratory alkalosis, from hyperventilation (anxiety, pain, hypoxia).

slides.title: A client admitted for alcohol withdrawal now (1500) has T 102° F, P 120, BP 164/
text: Question: A client admitted for alcohol withdrawal now (1500) has T 102° F, P 120, BP 164/100, profuse diaphoresis, hallucinations, nausea and vomiting (earlier vitals were near-normal with mild agitation). What action is appropriate?
A. Administer flumazenil.
B. Notify the PHCP.
C. Attempt to orient the client.
D. Increase the rate of the IV infusion.
Correct answer: B. Notify the PHCP.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:

This pattern indicates delirium tremens, a life-threatening emergency. The client needs more benzodiazepines, so notify the provider immediately. Flumazenil (a benzodiazepine antagonist) can trigger seizures.

slides.title: During a large-volume enema, the client’s abdomen becomes distended and rigid. W
text: Question: During a large-volume enema, the client’s abdomen becomes distended and rigid. What should the nurse do?
A. Reposition the client for better instillation.
B. Lower the enema fluid bag.
C. Ask the client to rate their pain level.
D. Discontinue the enema treatment.
Correct answer: D. Discontinue the enema treatment.
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
A distended, rigid abdomen suggests bowel perforation. Stop immediately and notify the provider.

slides.title: A female client was taught to collect a midstream urine specimen. Which statemen
text: Question: A female client was taught to collect a midstream urine specimen. Which statement requires additional teaching?
A. “I will remove the container before stopping the flow of urine.”
B. “Since I’m right-handed, I will use my left hand to spread the labia.”
C. “I will use the towelette to cleanse the area using a back-and-forth motion.”
D. “I will start to urinate in the toilet before urinating into the container.”
Correct answer: C. “I will use the towelette to cleanse the area using a back-and-forth motion.”
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Cleanse from front to back, using a new wipe each time. Back-and-forth spreads organisms toward the urethra.

slides.title: A client with Addison disease is at risk for Addisonian crisis. Which action sho
text: Question: A client with Addison disease is at risk for Addisonian crisis. Which action should the nurse take?
A. Restrict fluid intake.
B. Administer hydrocortisone.
C. Provide a low-carbohydrate diet.
D. Monitor the client’s ADH levels.
Correct answer: B. Administer hydrocortisone.
Topic: Endocrine & Metabolic
notes: Rationale:
Addison disease = cortisol/aldosterone deficiency; crisis causes hypotension, hypoglycemia, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia. Treatment is IV hydrocortisone and fluids, not restriction.

text: Question: Which finding should the nurse instruct parents to report after their child’s tonsillectomy?
A. Odor to the breath.
B. Persistent earache.
C. Mouth breathing.
D. Temperature of 99.4° F.
Correct answer: B. Persistent earache.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:

Bad breath and mouth breathing are expected after tonsillectomy, and a low-grade temp is normal. Persistent earache may signal infection and needs to be reported (also report frequent swallowing and bright red bleeding).

text: Question: A telemetry client continues to develop the rhythm shown (irregularly irregular, narrow QRS, no distinct P waves — atrial fibrillation). What should the nurse plan?
A. Prepare to administer digoxin.
B. Initiate transcutaneous pacing.
C. Defibrillate the client.
D. Administer IV atropine.
Correct answer: A. Prepare to administer digoxin.
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:

Atrial fibrillation with a stable client is treated with rate control (digoxin, β-blockers, calcium channel blockers) and anticoagulation. Pacing/atropine are for bradycardia, and defibrillation is for VF/pulseless VT. (Strip was an image.)

slides.title: Which signs and symptoms of peritonitis in peritoneal dialysis should the nurse
text: Question: Which signs and symptoms of peritonitis in peritoneal dialysis should the nurse discuss? 1 Hypoactive bowel sounds 2 Rebound abdominal tenderness 3 Amber urine 4 Nausea and vomiting 5 Cloudy or opaque outflow 6 Diarrhea 7 Bradycardia
Correct answer: D. 1, 2, 4, 5
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
Peritonitis: cloudy effluent, abdominal pain/rebound tenderness, fever, N/V, hypoactive bowel sounds (ileus), and tachycardia. Not bradycardia.

slides.title: A client suspected of having a retinal detachment of the LEFT eye. Which stateme
text: Question: A client suspected of having a retinal detachment of the LEFT eye. Which statement is consistent?
A. “I feel as if a curtain has been pulled down over my right eye.”
B. “I have lost the central part of my vision.”
C. “I am experiencing a sharp pain in my eye.”
D. “I see floating dark spots in my left eye.”
Correct answer: D. “I see floating dark spots in my left eye.”
Topic: Neuro, Eyes & Ortho
notes: Rationale:
Retinal detachment is painless with floaters, flashes, and a curtain/veil in the affected eye. Central vision loss suggests macular degeneration.

slides.title: The nurse has an order to remove intermittent sutures from an abdominal wound. W
text: Question: The nurse has an order to remove intermittent sutures from an abdominal wound. Which action should the nurse take?
A. Remove each suture in order from top to bottom.
B. Cut the suture by lifting it with forceps and cutting as close to the skin as possible.
C. Send the removed sutures to the lab for culture and sensitivity.
D. Apply adhesive strips after each suture is removed.
Correct answer: B. Cut the suture by lifting it with forceps and cutting as close to the skin as possible.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:

Lift the knot, cut close to the skin on the side opposite the knot, and pull gently so no exposed (contaminated) suture is dragged through tissue. Remove alternating sutures first, then apply strips as needed.

slides.title: A client with a pulmonary embolism on heparin. Which lab value requires immediat
text: Question: A client with a pulmonary embolism on heparin. Which lab value requires immediate attention?
A. PT 12 seconds
B. aPTT 60 seconds
C. Hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL
D. Platelets 100,000/mm³
Correct answer: D. Platelets 100,000/mm³
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
A falling platelet count (<100,000 or >50% drop) suggests heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT). Stop heparin and notify the provider. aPTT 60 s is therapeutic (1.5–2.5× control).

text: Question: A client has deep partial-thickness burns to the lower torso, both forearms, and thighs from a hot grease spill. Which action is a priority?
A. Maintaining a warm environment.
B. Inserting an indwelling urinary catheter.
C. Preparing to intubate the client.
D. Inspecting for signs of inhalation injury.
Correct answer: B. Inserting an indwelling urinary catheter.
Topic: Burns, Trauma & Emergencies
notes: Rationale:

This is a large burn (~30%+ TBSA) needing fluid resuscitation, and hourly urine output (≥30 mL/hr) is the best indicator that resuscitation is adequate. A scald from hot grease has no inhalation mechanism. (Key per source.)

Conflicting answer: the same question in the outside (not Galen) set "Comp C Highlights" gives a different answer: "Inspecting for signs of inhalation injuries.". Yours here is "Inserting an indwelling urinary catheter.". The two keys cannot both be what your instructor wants; check this one against your class materials.
